Elena_support: heads up — multiple customers (Acme, BlueWave) reporting p99 API latency spikes in eu1 since ~00:10 UTC. Support seeing 504s and backend timeouts. Can SRE/infra triage? :eyes:
Tiago_sre: on it. any correlation to recent infra changes?
Elena_support: customers say there was a host kernel rollout last night. I also see a flurry of alerts from borda-proxy about slow backend responds.
Raj_oncall: I’m seeing increased host-level io wait on several GPU hosts. topo: node-eu1-gpu-07, -08, -09. vmstat shows high wa and iotop shows NVMe queue depths spiking.
Lisa_infra: checking cluster ops history — kernel 6.1.12-rt rolled at 23:50 UTC to eu1 fleet (autoupdate). also a small nvme firmware bump got staged to the same nodes at 23:55.
Maria_prodeng: reproduction attempt on node-eu1-gpu-07: running short random reads causes p95 read latency to jump to ~60ms, p99 > 200ms. baseline last week was p99 ~8ms.
Maria_prodeng: paste logs:
```
[00:12:02] nvme0: sq 0 cq 0 completion latency hist: 99% 210ms  max 480ms
[00:12:03] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
fio: read: IOPS=2k, lat (usec): 99.9th=212345
```
Tiago_sre: that looks like host-side IO stalls, not model runtime. could be driver/kernel behavior interacting with nvme firmware.
Elena_support: customers are threatening to cut traffic, one has a hard SLO. we need mitigation plan fast.
Raj_oncall: immediate mitigations I can take: 1) cordon+drain the worst hosts from serving, 2) shift traffic away from eu1 region to eu2 canaries, 3) revert kernel on a small canary pool.
Lisa_infra: I can trigger a targeted rollback for 3 nodes (07-09) if approved. rollback command (apt-based hosts): `apt-get install linux-image-5.15.0-rc3 && update-grub && reboot` — will schedule for 2-3 node canary first.
Tiago_sre: before rebooting, try disabling the firmware NVMe QoS feature that's been flaky: `echo 0 > /sys/module/nvme_core/parameters/enable_io_queuing` (dry-run on canary) and set `echo noop > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler` to see if latency normalizes. do we have permission to run that?
Lisa_infra: copying commands to run on canary nodes now. will also pin irq affinity to avoid CPU stealing: `for d in /proc/irq/*/smp_affinity_list; do echo 0 > $d; done` (will restrict interrupts to cpu0 temporarily).
Elena_support: please coordinate — I'll tell Acme we’re doing canary rollback + traffic shift, ETA 20m for initial impact.
Raj_oncall: traffic shift done: routed 30% of eu1 traffic to eu2 canaries, monitoring.
Maria_prodeng: after disabling nvme io_queuing on node-eu1-gpu-07 p99 dropped from 210ms -> 18ms within 90s. I/O errors subsided in logs.
Tiago_sre: good signal. can we apply the nvme param change across the affected pool while we schedule kernel rollback? that avoids reboots.
Lisa_infra: applying parameter to nodes 07-09 now (via ansible adhoc). will watch for side effects.
deploy-bot: scheduled job: ansible-playbook apply-nvme-mitigation.yml -> hosts:[node-eu1-gpu-07,08,09] queued by lisa_infra at 00:35 UTC.
Raj_oncall: customers reporting improved p99s. Acme: p99 down to 22ms, errors cleared.
Elena_support: noted. next steps: 1) keep nvme param change as short-term mitigation, 2) run regression bisect between kernel 6.1.11 -> 6.1.12 and nvme fw variant, 3) prepare safe rollback playbook if regression confirmed, 4) schedule postmortem.
Tiago_sre: I'll own bisect. Maria, can you send the fio job + exact runner script to reproduce? put it in /incidents/1736001234/repro.sh (internal).
Maria_prodeng: done — `fio --name=randread --rw=randread --bs=4k --iodepth=32 --numjobs=4 --runtime=60 --filename=/dev/nvme0n1` — that reproduces the spike on affected hosts.
Elena_support: thanks all. I'll update customers and close the escalation once bisect confirms root cause and a rollback plan is scheduled. :thumbsup:
